catalog_quote: Sezo is a tone language. It is not a pitch-accent language because the location of a high pitch in a given word class is not predictable. According to Fox (2000: 179), a pitch-accent language ‘involves the use of pitch in an accentual function, i.e. to give prominence to one particular element […]’. Pitch-accent is assigned to either a prominent or a stressed syllable (Yip 2002:276). In Sezo, however, lexical items of comparable syllable structure can be divided into different groups only by their pitch variation. A word may not involve a high pitch at all.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Sezo has lexical tone (two level tones H and L, with LH and HL contours only on bimoraic syllables); it is explicitly not a pitch accent language: the position of a high pitch within a word of a given class is lexically unpredictable, and some words carry no high tone at all. The article never describes word stress or any predictable prominence; the deciding statement is about accent/pitch accent, not stress as such.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the article treats tone processes (downdrift, downstep, contour formation, H spreading) but no stress or prominence rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level; tone inventory established on disyllabic nouns/adjectives in citation form (root + terminal vowel) and on 2sg imperative verbs (pp. 56-57); data from Begi and Guddattu Qondala districts and Asosa, 2011-2014.
new_statements.first_reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.identity_note: Sezo = Seze (seze1235, ISO sze; endonym Seez Waani per Desta 2023 abstract), Non-Gonga Mao, spoken in Begi and Guddattu Qondala districts, West Wollega, Oromia. The source describes the language as a whole (no dialect named); data were gathered in villages of those districts and in Asosa. Caution: the same author's 2007 MA / 2010 VDM book is on 'Diddessa Mao', which is Bambassi/Northern Mao (bamb1262), not Seze.

tone_statements.citation: Girma Mengistu Desta. 2016. Tone in Sezo. In Binyam Sisay Mendisu & Janne Bondi Johannessen (eds.), Multilingual Ethiopia: Linguistic Challenges and Capacity Building Efforts, Oslo Studies in Language 8(1), 55-82. Oslo: University of Oslo. DOI 10.5617/osla.4419
tone_statements.quote: Sezo is a two-tone language. The two tones—high (H) and low (L), are able to occur on both monomoraic and bimoraic syllables. ... In addition to the level tones, Sezo shows rising LH and falling HL contour tones on some nouns, adjectives and verbs. But these are attested only on bimoraic syllables—syllables consisting of long vowels. ... In this study, contour tones are analyzed as fusions of the two level tones for various reasons.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 3 'The inventory of tones', p. 56 and p. 59
tone_statements.summary: Two level tones H and L; LH/HL contours only on long-vowel (bimoraic) syllables, analysed as H+L sequences; downstep triggered by floating L; tone also marks declarative vs interrogative.
